newsitem.title: USA: Non-OPEC oil production seen rising - consultants.
newsitem.headline: Non-OPEC oil production seen rising - consultants.

text.p: Oil production from non-OPEC countries is expected to rise by 1.4 million to 1.5 million barrels per day this year, industry consultants said on Thursday.

The higher production from the non-OPEC countries will go a long way toward meeting increased demand of 1.8 million to 2.0 million barrels per day (mbpd) projected this year, consultants with Arthur Andersen and Cambridge Energy Research Associates said.
Oil demand worldwide last year rose 1.76 mbpd, or 2.5 percent to a record annual average of 72.22 mbpd, the firms said in their annual world oil trends outlook.

OPEC oil production last year averaged 25.77 mbpd, a 3.1 percent increase from 1995 and the highest level since 1980, the firms said. Non-OPEC production rose 0.71 mbpd or 2 percent, led by a 0.32 mbpd increase from Norway and 0.25 mbpd increase from Mexico, the firms said
"United States production continued its slow but steady decline, down 0.07 mbpd from 1995 levels," the firms said.
